subject: MedSys POC hosting options — recap & action plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Turner <a.turner@medsys.org>, James Park <j.park@medsys.org>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0000
Subject: MedSys POC hosting options — recap & next steps

Hi Aisha / James —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path for the PoC so we can choose the right hosting mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call highlights (short):
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference into MedSys clinical-summaries flow (low-latency short generations, <250ms target median).
- Data residency: production must live in US (initial POC can use redacted data).
- Compliance: SOC 2 and audit logging are mandatory for production; procurement will need evidence.
- Scale: expected steady ~200 qps at peak for the first month; potential to double after go-live.

Options discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to start; good for functional validation and UX checks. Would require strict redaction until SOC 2 evidence is shared.
2) Dedicated capacity — predictable throughput and isolation; good if latency/throughput need is immediate and you want reserved GPUs.
3) Private VPC/on-prem — required only if procurement/legal insists on customer-managed network and KMS; longer lead time (contracts + infra).

Proposed PoC approach (low friction, 4 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): agree on scope + sign minimal SOW (covers trial data treatment) — Redwood to provide SOC 2 evidence bundle.
- Week 1–2: Functional POC on Hosted API with redacted datasets + synthetic load tests. Measure latencies, token costs, and quality on our eval set.
- Week 3: If throughput/latency issues appear, spin up Dedicated trial nodes (2-week reserve) to compare.
- Week 4: Consolidate results, recommend path to production (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) and present to stakeholders.

Success criteria (to be finalized with you):
- 95th percentile tail latency ≤ 400ms (target median <250ms)
- Accuracy / hallucination metrics within agreed baseline on sample prompts
- Total projected inference cost below threshold (TBD by procurement)

Action items from Redwood:
- Share PoC scope doc + SOC 2 evidence (I attached the scope, Grace will send the SOC files).
- Spin up a Hosted API sandbox and provide API keys for the PoC.

Could you confirm the proposed timeline and whether procurement needs a named contract before we start the Hosted API sandbox?

Thanks —
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: redwood-poc-scope.pdf (PDF)]

From: Aisha Turner <a.turner@medsys.org>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Park <j.park@medsys.org>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:35:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MedSys POC hosting options — recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: 4 weeks sounds reasonable, but Procurement needs a short SOW + limited-time trial agreement before we accept keys that will touch any customer data, even redacted.
- Data treatment: For the first two weeks we will run only de-identified clinical notes. If the POC requires PHI, that will push us to Private VPC and will need legal signoff.
- Security asks: SOC 2 report + pen test summary + retention policy. We also need an outline of your logging and audit capabilities.
- Throughput: 200 qps peak is correct; please include burst guidance (we may spike to 400 qps briefly).

Next steps on our side: I will introduce procurement (procurement@medsys.org) to your contracts contact and coordinate a quick review. James will engage if we need architecture-level changes.

If you can get the Hosted sandbox available behind a trial agreement/by-EULA we can start Week 1 with de-identified data. Otherwise we will need a Dedicated trial or Private evaluation — which would add ~2–3 weeks.

Aisha
Product Lead, MedSys Clinical AI
a.turner@medsys.org

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0000
Subject: MedSys PoC path confirmed — Hosted sandbox + contingency plan

Aisha / James — thanks for the quick turnaround and the procurement heads-up. Per our internal sync (Grace / Stephanie / Vivek), here's the agreed-on, minimally invasive path so we can start next week: 

1) Immediate: Redwood to send a 1-week temporary trial agreement (SOW + EULA-lite) and SOC 2 evidence bundle by EOD today. Procurement can review; the agreement limits the data types allowed (de-identified only).
2) Sandbox: if procurement signs the trial agreement, we will provision a Hosted API sandbox in us-east-1 with pre-set rate limits and an observability dashboard. Expected provisioning: 24 hours.
3) Load test & validation (Week 1–2 on sandbox): MedSys runs functional validation with de-identified data and synthetic load to exercise 200–400 qps bursts. Redwood will collect latency, cost, and quality metrics and deliver a mid-point report.
4) Contingency: if perf fails to meet requirements or procurement forbids Hosted, we will spin up a 2-week Dedicated trial (reserved nodes) and redo the load tests. This adds ~4 business days for infra prep and a modest trial fee (we will include numbers in the SOW).
5) Private VPC: only if Legal requires customer-controlled network/KMS. This will require enterprise contracting and ~3–4 weeks lead time.

Action items / owners: 
- Redwood: send trial agreement + SOC bundle (Ben / Grace / Stephanie) — by EOD today.
- MedSys: procurement review (procurement@medsys.org) and confirmation of allowed data types — by Mon 24 Aug.
- Redwood infra: prepare sandbox template and observability link (Vivek) — provision in 24 hours once agreement signed.

I'll attach the PoC scope and the SOC checklist again. Looking forward to getting the sandbox running — this path keeps time-to-value low while giving Procurement the controls they asked for.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
